findings.title: Premise cascade confuses skipping a criticism with rejecting its component
findings.description: A root finding challenges whether a planned component should exist. Skipping that criticism makes no edit and leaves the component in the plan. The dependency rule nevertheless treats Skip/Defer as making the component unsettled and offers to resolve related findings together; Apply is conversely described as the premise holding even when the proposed fix removes the component. This reverses the distinction between rejecting a review finding and rejecting proposed product scope.

Walkthrough explicitly defines Skip as no side effects; synthesis defines rejection as dissolving the component premise. Reviewer prompts formulate criticisms and concrete suggested fixes, not component-acceptance ballots.
findings.recommendation: Separate finding disposition from the resulting scope decision. Re-evaluate dependents against the actual accepted edit or explicit scope decision; Skip alone must not imply component removal or resolve its outstanding concerns.
findings.refactor_hint: Use explicit decision outcomes and dependency predicates over resulting plan state rather than over generic Apply/Skip/Defer labels.
findings.limits: Instruction-level contradiction only. Cascading requires separate user confirmation and independence safeguards may prevent some incorrect links; no actual suppressed finding or agent execution reproduced. Cross-unit dedup pending.
